plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on upright stems above blue-green strap-like leaves. Hundreds of cultivars exist, ranging from single early types to fringed, parrot, and double forms. It peaks in the Northern Hemisphere in mid to late April.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late spring (March to May)
plants.location: Temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens, especially the Netherlands, northern Europe, and North America; native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: During the Dutch 'Tulip Mania' of the 1630s, a single rare bulb could cost more than a luxurious canal house in Amsterdam.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose clusters of pea-like flowers appear directly on bare branches and even on the trunk before the heart-shaped leaves emerge. It is a favorite of early-season pollinators and a classic sign of spring in woodlands and gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid spring (late March to late April)
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, southern Ontario, and northern Mexico; widely planted elsewhere
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a mild, tangy flavor, and they're often added to salads or used as a garnish.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous, twining woody vine producing long, pendulous racemes of fragrant, pea-like flowers that open all at once before the leaves fully develop. It is often trained over pergolas, arbors, and walls and can live for decades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May)
plants.location: Native to China; cultivated in Japan, Europe, and the United States
plants.funFact: Chinese wisteria twines counterclockwise, while Japanese wisteria (Wisteria floribunda) twines clockwise, which helps tell them apart even without flowers.

plants.name: Nemophila menziesii
plants.description: A low-growing annual wildflower with delicate, bowl-shaped sky-blue flowers that have white centers and tiny dark speckles. It carpets grasslands and open hillsides during good rainfall years and is also grown in gardens and rock gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to late spring (February to May)
plants.location: California and Baja California; naturalized in parts of Japan and Europe where it is cultivated en masse
plants.funFact: At Hitachi Seaside Park in Japan, millions of baby blue eyes bloom in late April, turning entire hills into a sea of blue.
